verdict: Concur with no movement difference established for the bounded 1.14.3→1.14.4 player paths, with a material completeness qualification: the comparison omits the two-stage ServerPlayer correction call order.

findings.evidence: 1.14.3 LivingEntity.stopRiding captures old vehicle, calls super.stopRiding, and invokes server-only method_6038 only if old vehicle is nonnull and relation changed (LivingEntity.java:2322-2327). 1.14.4 has the same guard/order with findStandUpPosition (LivingEntity.java:2325-2330). Generic Entity.stopRiding detaches by nulling vehicle then removing passenger in both. Paired placement method bodies preserve the same neighbor ordering, candidate math, collision/standable/water tests, fallbacks, and boat/non-boat branch.

Portal block invokes entity portal handler. Server portal tick transition gate is !hasVehicle() in 1.14.3 and !isPassenger() in 1.14.4; these query the same vehicle relation. No portal-triggered generic dismount or separate portal dismount predicate found in the bounded dispatch.

During ServerPlayer stopRiding, super.stopRiding invokes the LivingEntity placement helper. Its final requestTeleport/teleportTo dynamically dispatches to ServerPlayerEntity.requestTeleport / ServerPlayer.teleportTo and the network handler, sending correction 1 at the computed stand-up XYZ (old LivingEntity.java:1715, ServerPlayerEntity.java:1082-1083; new LivingEntity.java:1718, ServerPlayer.java:1087-1088). Once super returns, ServerPlayer stopRiding checks relation changed plus nonnull handler/connection and sends correction 2 at current XYZ (old ServerPlayerEntity.java:760-766; new ServerPlayer.java:764-770). This does not establish a version difference, but the omitted first correction is material to exact call order.
findings.result: Same two-correction behavior in both versions; lane text should include it

findings.evidence: Both network handler overloads use empty relative-flag sets for this path (old ServerPlayNetworkHandler.java:808-825; new ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.java:860-877), record target XYZ, update server-side player XYZ, and send packet with relative components subtracted only when explicitly requested. The called path uses empty set, hence absolute XYZ/angles. Both client handlers require main-thread execution, for each XYZ axis add current position only if relative; otherwise set the corresponding old render coordinate and zero that velocity component; relative angles add to current yaw/pitch, then call the absolute position writer and acknowledge. Old ClientPlayNetworkHandler.java:641-688; new ClientPacketListener.java:659-706.
findings.topic: Server packet absolute flags and direct client XYZ
